findings.explanation: The PR adds filtering by workspace__slug and project_id to the Issue query (line 1121), which is a security improvement. However, the base code at line 1121 fetches issues by id__in without any workspace or project filtering, creating an IDOR vulnerability. A user with ADMIN or MEMBER role in one project could modify issues from other projects by providing their IDs directly in the request. The @allow_permission decorator only validates that the user has the correct role in the specified project (via kwargs['project_id']), but does not constrain the actual data being queried. The PR fixes this by adding the missing workspace and project filters to the query, ensuring users can only modify issues that belong to their authorized project and workspace.

allow_permission decorator validates user role permissions at the project level but does not constrain the queryset itself; the decorator ensures the user has correct permissions but the view must still filter the actual data being queried

findings.suggested_fix: Add workspace__slug and project_id filters to the Issue query to ensure users can only modify issues within their authorized workspace and project scope. This is what the PR correctly implements at line 1121.
